questions.prompt: How can never help with exhaustive union handling?
options: Assign the remaining value to never so a newly added union member causes a type error.
Use never as the default value for every variable.
It automatically adds missing switch cases at runtime.
It disables diagnostics for the switch.
questions.answer_key: Assign the remaining value to never so a newly added union member causes a type error.
questions.explanation: An exhaustive check makes incomplete handling easier to detect when a union changes.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Exhaustiveness Checking”?
options: The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with handling every union member and checked against its intended contract.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with handling every union member and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Handling every union member”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Exhaustiveness Checking”?
options: Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check using never to detect missing cases, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume exhaustive switch statements is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
questions.answer_key: Check using never to detect missing cases, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Using never to detect missing cases”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
